analysis.note: Corrected from the earlier compound stem vyavasāyātmaka: the verifier rightly notes that vyavasāyātmaka as Stri/Prathama/Eka would give vyavasāyātmakā, whereas the printed/commented form is vyavasāyātmikā. This is the feminine -ā stem corresponding to -ātmaka/-ātmikā. I retain the bahuvrīhi analysis on semantic and commentarial grounds, though the verifier logged the relation as unsupported.

verification.detail: compound stem vyavasāyātmikā as Stri/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Printed together with iha as ekeha by ā + i → e sandhi; Śaṅkara emphasizes ekā eva, “one alone.”
Printed together with ekā as ekeha; Śaṅkara takes iha as iha śreyo-mārge, “here, on the path to the highest good.”
Vocative address to Arjuna; the bhāṣya repeats it without further gloss. The verifier reported a tool_error, not a derivational contradiction, so the analysis is retained.

verification.detail: compound stem kuru-nandana as Pum/Sambodhana/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Predicate adjective agreeing with buddhayaḥ. The bhāṣya’s printed bahvvayaḥ is likely an orthographic error for bahvyaḥ, but the immediately following yāsāṃ construction establishes the bahuvrīhi sense. The verifier reported a tool_error and logged the relation as unsupported; I retain the analysis because Śaṅkara explicitly gives the bahuvrīhi-style vigraha.

verification.detail: compound stem bahu-śākhā as Stri/Prathama/Bahu: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Explanatory particle, here rendered “for”; in sandhi before anantāḥ it appears as hy.
Predicate adjective agreeing with buddhayaḥ; Śaṅkara explains the endlessness by proliferation through branch-distinctions.
Plural subject of the second hemistich.
Genitive dependent on buddhayaḥ: “the understandings of the avyavasāyins.” Śaṅkara defines these as those lacking discriminative understanding born of valid knowledge.

justifications.decision: The compound is not taken as “effortful” or merely “purposive”; Śaṅkara explicitly equates vyavasāyātmikā with niścaya-svabhāvā and connects this buddhi with valid cognition.
justifications.chosen: vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ = “understanding whose nature is settled determination.”

evidence.translation: Because it is produced by a correct means of knowledge.

justifications.decision: ekā is emphatic, not merely numeral, and iha is not “in this world” but “on the śreyas-path” in Śaṅkara’s construal.
options_considered: “one” as a mere count without emphasis
“one alone here/on the path to the highest good”
justifications.chosen: ekā iha = “one alone here, on the path to the highest good.”

evidence.translation: Here, on the path to the highest good.

justifications.decision: The compound qualifies buddhayaḥ and is not an independent noun phrase “many branches”; Śaṅkara gives the yāsām-bahuvrīhi vigraha and glosses it as bahu-bhedāḥ.
options_considered: “having many scriptural branches” in a narrow Vedic-recensional sense

evidence.quote: tā buddhayo bahu-śākhāḥ bahvvayaḥ śākhāḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ bahu-śākhāḥ, bahu-bhedā ity etat
evidence.translation: Those understandings are ‘many-branched’: those whose branches are many (printed bahvvayaḥ, likely for bahvyaḥ), that is, many-divided.
But the other ones are contrary understandings.

justifications.decision: The endlessness is the unlimited proliferation of these contrary understandings by branch and sub-branch, not merely an abstract epithet; Śaṅkara explicitly says the buddhayaḥ are anantāḥ by pratiśākhā-bheda.
justifications.chosen: anantāḥ = “endless,” predicated of the plural buddhayaḥ.

evidence.translation: For by the distinction of each branch the understandings too are endless.

evidence.quote: yāsāṃ śākhā-bheda-pracāra-vaśāt ananto 'pāro 'nuparataḥ saṃsāro nitya-pratato vistīrṇo bhavati
evidence.translation: Because of the spread of their branch-distinctions, saṃsāra becomes endless, boundless, unceasing, ever-extended, and vast.

justifications.decision: Although the dictionary may suggest ‘inactive/negligent,’ Śaṅkara defines the avyavasāyins epistemically: they lack pramāṇa-generated viveka-buddhi. The genitive answers keṣām, “of whom?” and depends on buddhayaḥ.
justifications.chosen: avyavasāyinām = “of the irresolute,” specifically those lacking valid-knowledge-born discriminative understanding.

evidence.translation: Of whom? Of the avyavasāyins, that is, of those bereft of discriminative understanding born of a means of knowledge.

justifications.decision: The commentary only repeats the address; the compound relation is decided grammatically from Kuru + nandana as a standard vocative address to Arjuna.
options_considered: taking kuru as an imperative of √kṛ
taking nandana as a separate nominative
justifications.chosen: kuru-nandana is a vocative ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, “O delight/descendant of the Kurus.”

one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render vyavasāya as “effort” and avyavasāyinām as “inactive/negligent”; Śaṅkara instead makes the contrast one of pramāṇa-born determinative understanding versus the lack of such discriminative understanding.
It might translate iha simply as “in this world”; Śaṅkara narrows it to “on the path to the highest good” (śreyo-mārga).
It might miss that bahu-śākhāḥ is explicitly a bahuvrīhi, “those whose branches are many,” glossed as “many-divided,” and that anantāḥ refers to the endless proliferation of these contrary buddhis.
analyzer_disagreements: The ByT5 api_seg gives vyavasāya_ātmakā, but the unit text and the local analyses read vyavasāyātmikā; I now analyze the printed feminine compound stem as vyavasāyātmikā rather than the mfn stem vyavasāyātmaka, since the latter derives vyavasāyātmakā.
ByT5 segments vyavasāyātmikā and bahu-śākhāḥ into their members; per instruction, I give each as a single compound subanta with a whole-compound stem and add samāsa analysis.
ByT5 treats kuru and nandana as separate compound/member tokens; I analyze the printed address kuru-nandana as one vocative tatpuruṣa compound.
mula: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana | bahu-śākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām
commentary_lines: vyavasāyātmikā niścaya-svabhāvā ekā eva buddhir itara-viparīta-buddhi-śākhā-bhedasya vādhikā, samyak-pramāṇa-janitatvāt, iha śreyo-mārge |

he kurunandana ! yāḥ punar itarā viparīta-buddhayaḥ, yāsāṃ śākhā-bheda-pracāra-vaśāt ananto 'pāro 'nuparataḥ saṃsāro nitya-pratato vistīrṇo bhavati, pramāṇa-janita-viveka-buddhi-nimitta-vaśāc ca uparatāsv ananta-bheda-buddhiṣu saṃsāro 'py uparamate tā buddhayo bahu-śākhāḥ bahvvayaḥ śākhāḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ bahu-śākhāḥ, bahu-bhedā ity etat |
